This experiment isolates the error introduced by the rational approximation
of the **discrete** fractional operator. The rational solution is computed
with the existing shifted sparse solver at every time step. Its reference
is backward Euler with the exact fractional power of the same assembled
FEM operator, evaluated through a complete numerical generalized
eigendecomposition. No identity about projected continuum eigenfunctions
is assumed.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, cache = FALSE, message = FALSE)
source(here::here("sourceifupdated.R"))
source_if_updated("fun/fractional_evolution")
source_if_updated("fun/graphs_and_meshes")
source_if_updated("fun/reference_experiments")
source_if_updated("fun/isolated_rational_convergence")
```

# The comparison

The physical equation is
\[
u_t+\nu(\kappa^2-\Delta_\Gamma)^{\alpha/2}u=f,
\qquad u_0=10e_5,\qquad f(t)=10\sin(\pi t)e_7.
\]
Both discrete evolutions receive the same initial vector, physical forcing
load, diffusion coefficient, and interval-averaged sine forcing. For
\(C=\texttt{graph\$mesh\$C}\) and \(L=\kappa^2C+G\), the full
numerical eigensystem satisfies
\[
LV=CV\Lambda,\qquad V^\top CV=I.
\]
The exact-discrete reference uses
\[
U_h^{k+1}=V\operatorname{diag}\left(
\frac{1}{1+\tau\nu\lambda_j^{\alpha/2}}\right)
V^\top(CU_h^k+\tau F^{k+1}).
\]
The primary measured error is
\[
E_{\mathrm{rat}}(m)=\left[
\tau\sum_{k=1}^N(U_h^k-U_{h,m}^k)^\top C(U_h^k-U_{h,m}^k)
\right]^{1/2}.
\]
This is the exact time integral between their common right-constant
reconstructions, up to arithmetic error. There is no reference space/time
quadrature. The initial and forcing hat loads are integrated analytically;
the latter is an explicit change from the fine-mesh forcing-load
approximation in the old continuum-error notebook.

Spatial and temporal discretizations are shared by both solutions and
therefore contribute no independent continuum-error floor. They still
change the finite-dimensional experiment, so their influence on the
observed curve is checked by refinement.

# Parameters and private run

The defaults preserve the original horizon \(T=10^{-3}\),
\(\kappa=4\), data and alpha values. `coefficient_source = "package"` uses the original
tables and \(m=1,2,3,4\). Choosing `"computed"` reads the CSV and uses
\(m=1,\ldots,8\). The base mesh is \(h=10^{-2}\) and the target step is
\(10^{-5}\). Space, time, and both are independently halved. These are
moderate problems suitable for a complete eigendecomposition.

`workers` schedules all alpha/order pairs together within each scenario.
The eigensystem is reused across parameters, and an exact reference
history is computed once per alpha/time grid. The size guards reject
accidentally choosing the large dense problems of the original notebook.

```{r parameters}
study_parameters <- if (is.null(params$settings))
  isolated_m_parameters(params$coefficient_source, params$coefficient_file) else params$settings
# To change science settings, pass a modified settings list to
# render_isolated_m_notebook(parameters = settings). See the example below.

run_dir <- reference_experiment_run("m", study_parameters, params$run_id)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = paste0(file.path(run_dir, "notebook_figures"), "/"))
cat("Run ID:", basename(run_dir), "\nPrivate artifacts:", run_dir, "\n")
knitr::kable(study_parameters$scenarios)
cat("Coefficient source:", isolated_coefficient_source(study_parameters),
    "\nOrders:", paste(study_parameters$m, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (isolated_coefficient_source(study_parameters) == "computed")
  cat("CSV:", study_parameters$coefficient_file, "\nSHA-256:",
      study_parameters$coefficient_sha256, "\n")
```

To select the computed source, change `coefficient_source: package` to
`coefficient_source: computed` in this notebook's YAML and click Knit. The
renderer reads that setting and automatically selects orders 1--8. The
CSV path can be changed with `coefficient_file`. Alternatively, from R:

```{r computed-source-example, eval=FALSE}
settings <- isolated_m_parameters("computed")
render_isolated_m_notebook(parameters = settings, workers = 4L)
```

The CSV was generated by `tests/audit_rational_generation.m` in NAFDEMG's
`diffusion-parameter` branch, and a verbatim generator copy is included
in this branch at the same path. Computed values are selected at their exact
stored beta; MATLAB is not run and no interpolation/fallback is performed.
The artifact path and content hash distinguish these runs from package runs.

Results, figures, and diagnostics stay under
`~/Desktop/DOCS/NAFDEMG/diffusion_experiments/m/<run_id>/` (or the configured
`NAFDEMG_PRIVATE_DIR`). To reload an existing run, render with its `run_id`
and `execute = FALSE`. Metadata must match. Computing into an existing
results file is refused.

```{r compute}
result_file <- file.path(run_dir, "isolated_m_results.rds")
if (isTRUE(params$execute)) {
  if (file.exists(result_file)) stop("This run already has results; reload or use a fresh run ID.")
  results <- run_isolated_m_study(study_parameters, workers = params$workers,
    max_dimension = params$max_dimension, max_dense_mib = params$max_dense_mib,
    max_history_mib = params$max_history_mib)
  save_isolated_m_results(results, run_dir)
} else {
  if (!file.exists(result_file)) stop("No saved isolated result for this run ID.")
  results <- readRDS(result_file)
  stopifnot(identical(results$parameters, study_parameters))
}
```

# Measured error and fitted decay

Solid lines show the primary sparse-solver result. Open circles mark points
below the diagnostic numerical-resolution threshold. Dashed lines use the
bound exponent \(-2\pi\sqrt{1-\alpha/2}\), anchored at the first order.
Their vertical placement is not a proved bound constant. The natural-log
fit against \(\sqrt m\) across the selected orders is a finite-order measurement; it need
not equal the bound benchmark or be perfectly linear.

```{r plot, echo=FALSE}
plot <- isolated_m_error_plot(results)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(run_dir, "isolated_m_errors.png"), plot,
                width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 180, bg = "white")
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(run_dir, "isolated_m_errors.pdf"), plot,
                width = 10, height = 7, bg = "white")
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(run_dir, "isolated_m_errors.png"), rel_path = FALSE)
```

```{r base-errors, echo=FALSE}
base <- results$errors[results$errors$scenario == "base", ]
base <- base[order(base$alpha, base$m), ]
knitr::kable(base[, c("alpha", "m", "error", "product_error",
  "max_relative_rate_error_excited", "resolution_ratio")], digits = 10)
```

```{r slopes, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(results$slopes, digits = 6)
```

# Checks and diagnosis

The eigensystem is checked using generalized eigen-residuals and
\(C\)-orthogonality. The independent rational root-product recurrence in
the complete numerical eigenbasis checks the sparse implementation. At
\(\alpha=2\), rational approximation is bypassed; its measured difference
should be a numerical zero and provides an additional consistency control.

The diagnostic resolution ratio compares the product error with the larger
of the sparse/product disagreement and the alpha=2 control. This is an
empirical numerical indicator, not a certified error bound.

```{r diagnosis, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
for (paragraph in isolated_m_diagnosis(results)) cat(paragraph, "\n\n")
```

```{r numerical-checks, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(results$eigensystem_diagnostics, digits = 10)
knitr::kable(results$zero_controls[, c("scenario", "error", "product_error", "final_state_gap_C")],
             digits = 12)
beta_column <- if ("coefficient_beta_exact" %in% names(base))
  "coefficient_beta_exact" else "beta_exact_in_package_table"
knitr::kable(base[, c("alpha", "m", "absolute_error_disagreement", "relative_error_disagreement",
  beta_column, "beta_table_lower", "beta_table_upper")], digits = 10)
```

Package interpolation brackets are recorded because unavailable exact beta
values are obtained by linearly interpolating roots and factors. Computed
runs instead record exact beta matching. At higher orders, some errors can
fall below numerical resolution; those points remain visible and the
diagnosis distinguishes the all-order and resolved-only descriptive fits. A
plateau or increase in the scalar approximation error can survive removal
of spatial/time error floors. These runs retain the original source and
do not silently replace coefficients to obtain a preferred slope.

# Mesh and time sensitivity

The default reporting thresholds are a 2% relative change in the isolated
error and 0.05 absolute change in the fitted slope. Both the raw changes
and pass flags are saved. A failed sensitivity check calls for additional
investigation; it is not a failure of the exact-discrete comparison identity.

```{r refinements, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(results$refinement_errors, digits = 8)
knitr::kable(results$refinement_slopes, digits = 8)
```

# Reproducing and interpreting the run

The full formulas and implementation are in
`fun/isolated_rational_convergence.Rmd`. Run the regression checks with
`Rscript tests/check_isolated_m.R` from the project environment.

The RStudio Knit button uses a custom renderer that keeps the report in its
private run directory. From R, after loading the helpers, a fresh run is:

```{r usage, eval=FALSE}
settings <- isolated_m_parameters()
# settings$diffusion <- 2
render_isolated_m_notebook(parameters = settings, workers = 4L)
```

Reload a saved run with `render_isolated_m_notebook(run_id = "<saved ID>",
execute = FALSE)`. Pass its modified `parameters` list as well if its
scientific settings differ from the defaults. Metadata and package versions
must match. Reloading regenerates the report and figures from saved data
without overwriting the scientific results.

This study supports conclusions about the chosen discrete problem,
physical data, coefficients, and tested orders. It does not measure the
continuum error \(\|u-U_{h,m}^\tau\|\), certify uniform operator accuracy,
or establish an asymptotic rational approximation rate from these finitely many orders.
